races.name: HKJC World Pool Battaash Handicap

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old carries headgear (p) and has consistent recent form at this trip on good ground, with eight of nine comparable-going runs yielding a place; she is the lone confirmed pace-setter and her ability to control fractions without pressure is central to the race shape, though a STYLE_FIT flag hints she is operating slightly outside her most comfortable role.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of five on our figures, he struggled badly in a Group 1 at Ascot most recently, leaving plenty to prove on his return to handicap company. First-time cheekpieces on a colt whose best trip is 6f, though an official mark of 100 looks stiff.

runners_data.name: Comical Point
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for Andrew Balding and the colt has posted five consecutive places at six furlongs on good or similar — stepping back to five is the key question, but Sandown's stiff finish suits a horse that travels prominently and keeps finding; his seven-from-eight similar-going record underlines reliability.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at 6f on good ground, he pushed the winner close at Windsor last time, beaten half a length off a mark 2lb lower than today's. First-time tongue-tie and the booking of Ryan Moore strengthen the case for our top-rated runner here.

runners_data.name: Westport
runners_data.note: George Boughey's unbeaten-in-three lightly raced colt is a horse who wants to be forward — his three wins have all been made from the front or near it — and while the map places him in midfield because of the crowded prominent division, Billy Loughnane will likely seek to recover ground toward the pace; his 5f course-distance form is the most directly relevant in the field.
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last four starts show him in smart form; his Ascot handicap debut, where his draw left him unable to land a blow, can be forgiven. Those victories look solid, and he merits another chance here in a more accessible contest.

runners_data.name: Exclamation
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's filly has one win from thirteen comparable-ground runs and a patchy recent form string (-90190), and though she is a natural front-runner by inclination she has been repositioned on the map because Westport and Havana Hurricane are more likely to occupy those berths; Rossa Ryan will need to balance her desire to be forward against the risk of overcommitting energy early.
runners_data.comment: A three-quarter length success at Chester three starts back shows he can do it, but he has been highly inconsistent around that effort. Retained cheekpieces and a 2lb pull in the weights add interest, though his current official mark looks demanding.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's three-year-old is the sole hold-up horse and arrives on the back of a five-furlong good-ground win, but a 1-from-14 record on similar going illustrates how rarely the stars align; Ryan Kavanagh (5lb claim) needs a strongly-run race to get competitive, which is not the expected tempo in a five-runner field with one natural front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Returned to his best last time, drawing away to take a handicap by a length at Goodwood off a mark 6lb lower than today's. Acts well at this trip on good ground and is a reliable type; the concern is a trainer managing just one winner from 49 recent runners.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Hurricane is the one confirmed pace-maker in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressure her through the early furlongs on Sandown's stiff five, she can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop. Comical Point will track her from a prominent position, while Westport and Exclamation — both natural front-runners by inclination — are redistributed into a midfield role on the map because they cannot all occupy the same ground at the head of affairs; in practice Westport, who has won his last three and boasts the highest recent strike-rate, is the most likely of the two to push for a forward berth and may challenge Havana Hurricane for control. One And Gone is the lone hold-up runner and will be ridden to pick up whatever scraps the pace leaves at the finish. This race shape — an unhurried, uncontested early pace set by a single confirmed leader with the closers having to produce their effort against a moderate tempo — strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the pace, because the leader is never likely to be stretched early enough to stop and wait.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent striker
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Hurricane leads at a fair but unhurried gallop and the prominent trackers quicken off the steady tempo.
scenarios.body: If Havana Hurricane leads at a fair but unhurried gallop and the prominent trackers quicken off the steady tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace battle, leader fades late
scenarios.trigger: If Westport or Exclamation pushes Havana Hurricane into a contested, above-average early gallop.
scenarios.body: If Westport or Exclamation pushes Havana Hurricane into a contested, above-average early gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow pace, sprint-finish lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Hurricane is unusually cautious early and the field concertinas into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Havana Hurricane is unusually cautious early and the field concertinas into a sprint from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot early and One And Gone is produced with a well-timed late run off a strong gallop.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely hot early and One And Gone is produced with a well-timed late run off a strong gallop.

watchPoints.text: Westport's true running style means Billy Loughnane may push forward to contest the lead with Havana Hurricane — if that happens, watch for an unscheduled pace battle in the opening furlong that changes the entire race shape.

One And Gone needs a genuinely strong gallop to deliver from off the pace; if Havana Hurricane idles in front, One And Gone's hold-up position becomes a significant disadvantage with only five furlongs to make up the ground.

Comical Point drops from six furlongs to five for the first time in his recent campaign — watch in the final furlong to see whether the sharp Sandown finish tests his stamina or whether the shorter trip actually sharpens his finishing kick.

With only five runners on good ground at Sandown, draw and early position will be disproportionately influential — monitor how quickly each jockey moves to claim their natural running position from the gates before the field settles.

races.name: Coral Dragon Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's hold-up two-year-old has winning form on Good ground but has been placed only once in five starts; from the rear he needs a strong pace to deliver, and his recent run of 6th over 6f on Good suggests he may be finding his level.
runners_data.comment: Pushed to his limits at Ascot last time, finishing four lengths behind the leaders in a Listed contest having possibly reached his ceiling; acts at 6f on good to firm and good to soft, with stall nine providing a wide berth to navigate.

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Now the sole front-runner after Divine Whisper's withdrawal, Pat Cosgrave can exploit an uncontested lead on Good turf; his win came over 6f and dropping to 5f is the key question, but form figures of 1-3-4 show consistent competitiveness.
runners_data.comment: Won a maiden at Bath by three lengths last time having benefited from a drop in class, with his earlier course form here in Listed company given a further boost at Royal Ascot; the sharp 5f trip suits and he acts well on good ground.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has only the one run to her name — a promising second over this exact 5f Good trip — giving her an OR of 120 but minimal evidence of how she handles a field and traffic; the unknown ceiling is both her appeal and her risk.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well on debut at Goodwood, pulling away from a more experienced rival before going down by two lengths in a maiden; handles 5f on good ground and is likely to progress, though this is a significant step up in class for a once-raced colt.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: Three runs all over 5f on Good ground with a win and two placed efforts tells a consistent story; Rowan Scott rides and Nigel Tinkler sends him from 34 days off, but his form trajectory (7-1-2) suggests improvement is possible.
runners_data.comment: Still green under pressure at Beverley last time, narrowly denied by a short-head in a 2yo contest; acts well at 5f on good and fast ground and looks capable of further progress as that rawness irons out.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Winner of her most recent start over 5f on Good ground but opened her account at 15/1 on debut before bouncing back; Richard Spencer's lightly raced filly is genuinely unexposed, though a form string of just two runs makes projection hazardous.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a Group 2 at Ascot last time where the pace was simply too sharp at that level; has a speedy pedigree, acts at 5f on good ground and his trainer is currently in form, but the bar to clear here remains considerable.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount for Richard Hughes, and Bint Archange has placed twice in three starts on Good ground; she finished 27th on debut but has improved sharply since, and her prominent style fits the likely race shape though she carries the 5lb allowance.
runners_data.comment: Taken too forward in a Group 2 at Ascot last time and weakened well before the line; a fine prospect who acts at 5f on a sound surface and is capable of bouncing back, though the trainer is in a lean spell.

runners_data.name: Havana Flash
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners George Boughey's hold-up filly who ran just six days ago; her debut second over this course and distance on Good is highly relevant, and the quick turnaround is worth noting — Boughey runs her fit rather than fresh.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck on her second start at Lingfield last time after showing the benefit of her debut outing; a speedy pedigree with her dam successful at Listed level gives her appeal, though stall eight is a wide berth and this is a significant rise in class.

runners_data.name: Miss Lizzy
runners_data.note: Paddy Bradley rides for Charlie Fellowes, and Miss Lizzy's one win came over 6f at Sandown; her 5f Good-ground form shows a 4th and an 11th, making the trip here a minor concern, and a T14 strike rate of 1/18 is modest.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 at Ascot last time, a performance well within her capabilities at this level; acts at 5-6f on a sound surface and probably at her best over a slightly longer trip, though first-time tongue-tie could provide a boost.

runners_data.name: Divine Whisper
runners_data.note: Non-runner — George Boughey's Listed-class front-runner is absent, and her withdrawal materially changes the pace scenario, removing the one horse most likely to force a genuine early pace test on Bill The Bull.

races.paceDynamic: With Divine Whisper a non-runner, Bill The Bull is now the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Listed contest, and with no direct rival to chase him from the gates he can dictate a controlled, honest pace rather than an all-out burn. Ronson, It Dunt Marra, and Bint Archange all want to race prominently, meaning there will be competition for the slipstream positions behind Bill The Bull from the first stride, with traffic risk materialising around the 2f-3f mark as those four battle for the best ground. On Good turf at Sandown's straight 5f, a single front-runner setting a measured gallop rather than a true test tends to compress the field, keeping hold-up horses in contention but ultimately rewarding those close enough to pounce in the final furlong without burning fuel in the pack. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a fair but not scorching pace — tilts the advantage toward prominent-to-midfield types who can travel into the race, avoid the congestion between the prominent quartet, and produce a sustained late effort; pure closers will need things to go perfectly from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bill The Bull Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bill The Bull breaks cleanly, settles into an uncontested lead and sets a metronomic pace that rewards those tracking just off him.
scenarios.body: If Bill The Bull breaks cleanly, settles into an uncontested lead and sets a metronomic pace that rewards those tracking just off him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pack races keenly and the mid-race tempo becomes fast enough to string the field out, leaving room for late closers to finish through.
scenarios.body: If the pack races keenly and the mid-race tempo becomes fast enough to string the field out, leaving room for late closers to finish through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Congestion Assists Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the jostling between Ronson, It Dunt Marra, Bint Archange and Miss Lizzy in the first two furlongs creates trouble and disrupts all of them, freeing Bill The Bull to coast home.
scenarios.body: If the jostling between Ronson, It Dunt Marra, Bint Archange and Miss Lizzy in the first two furlongs creates trouble and disrupts all of them, freeing Bill The Bull to coast home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced, unexposed horses produces a step-change in performance beyond their current form lines.
scenarios.body: If one of the lightly raced, unexposed horses produces a step-change in performance beyond their current form lines.

watchPoints.text: Bill The Bull (Pat Cosgrave) — with Divine Whisper a non-runner he faces zero early pressure; watch if he gets the rail and settles, as an uncontested lead on Good ground over 5f can be nearly unassailable at this level.

Prominent congestion between Ronson, It Dunt Marra, and Bint Archange in the first furlong — three horses want the same ground directly behind Bill The Bull and traffic interference between the 3f and 2f marks is a genuine risk for all of them.

Havana Flash (Billy Loughnane) — ran only six days ago and now steps into Listed company; watch her pre-race demeanour and whether the quick turnaround has left any residual fatigue that undermines her hold-up finishing effort.

It Dunt Marra (Rossa Ryan) — with just one run on the clock and an OR of 120, she is the most unexposed horse in the field; watch how she handles the early jostle from a prominent position, as her debut was a lone-runner affair with no pack pressure.

Underdog (Saffie Osborne) — her debut was a distant 15th before winning next time; watch whether that debut experience now helps her handle the early pace and find a clean route through from midfield, as her form trajectory is steeply upward.

races.name: Tattersalls 40,000 Pound EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Collateral Damage
runners_data.comment: Showed genuine promise when landing a maiden at Catterick by a neck on debut and should continue to improve with that experience under his belt; bred to get beyond 7f and acts on good to soft, though stall eleven is a wide berth to overcome.

runners_data.name: Gymbaazy
runners_data.comment: Landed a maiden here by a neck on debut despite meeting interference, suggesting there is more to come with a cleaner passage; effective over 7f on good ground and with the trainer in excellent form, he is a live threat despite carrying a penalty.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.comment: Well held when stepped up in class in a novice at Goodwood last time under a penalty, and the rise to 7f is uncertain to suit on breeding; his form at 6f on good to soft has the most appeal, making this a stiff test.

runners_data.name: Beach Noir
runners_data.comment: A 25,000-guinea breeze-up purchase by Blackbeard and a half-brother to Only In Dreams, who showed ability at 12f; with no racecourse experience and the field setting a solid standard, he looks best watched on debut from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.comment: Well beaten late in a Group 2 at Ascot after racing prominently throughout, but this represents a significant drop in grade; effective at 6f on good and fast ground and if his stamina holds at 7f, he sets the form standard here.

runners_data.name: Dontlookbackinanga
runners_data.comment: A 92,000-guinea Acclamation colt, full-brother to Tabarrak who was high-class at 7f, with a dam that was smart at 8f and successful on her debut; the market should be informative on his first start, and the 7f trip looks well within his compass on breeding.

runners_data.name: Encounter
runners_data.comment: Held up by interference at a key stage last time yet still managed a two-length third here on his most recent start, which reads better than it appears; has speed in his pedigree but seems effective at 7f on good ground and remains a genuine player.

runners_data.name: Or Ever
runners_data.comment: A Mehmas colt, half-brother to Kindergarten who was notably capable at 6f; the stable has a decent record with first-time-out runners and a strong jockey booking is noteworthy, though he has no racecourse form to assess.

runners_data.name: Storm Blade
runners_data.comment: Showed some early promise when fourth on debut at Lingfield — beaten six lengths but still green throughout; bred to get around a mile and should improve with experience, though stall twelve is a wide draw and this stronger field is a big ask.

runners_data.name: The Balearic Sun
runners_data.comment: A 300,000-guinea Lope De Vega colt, half-brother to Berkshire Rocco who excelled at 15f, with a half-sister that landed a Listed race in Italy; the stable has a record of producing competitive debutants, though the dam was moderate at 8f and this is a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Walcourt
runners_data.comment: A 70,000-euro Churchill colt, half-brother to Sollertia, a very useful 7f performer, out of a dam who was talented at 8f; the stable's record with first-time-out runners is modest, making him harder to recommend on debut despite the appealing pedigree.

races.name: Davies Insurance Solutions Gala Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Boiling Point
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a recent Goodwood win on good ground and consistent OR=112 form, trained by K R Burke with James Doyle up; naturally wants to race prominently but this field has more pace than it can accommodate, so expect Boiling Point to sit slightly further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Ran too freely up front on soft ground at Epsom last time and paid for it late, finishing two lengths third; stays 10f well on a sound surface but has not been at his sharpest this season and the top weight is an added burden.

runners_data.name: Dividend
runners_data.note: Consistent Rossa Ryan mount for Dr Newland & Insole showing a 311253 string largely over 9-10f on good going — the style, record, and trip all align well for tracking Sallaal in second from the front of the chasing pack.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a Listed contest at Ascot last time in a performance that reads to form, and his progressive record around that level makes him a credible threat; first-time cheekpieces, acts on this ground and effective over today's trip, though this step up in class is the test.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Richard Hannon on this hold-up five-year-old, but her recent form (05-425) and a sim-going record of just 7/15 on ground this firm present genuine concerns; she needs a stronger pace than Sallaal is likely to set to get into the race from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Back in form when beaten three lengths in a Listed contest at Ascot last time, suggesting there is a bit more to offer over a slightly longer trip; effective at 8-10f on any ground with a top jockey back aboard, though he faces stiff opposition here.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhyme
runners_data.note: K R Burke's six-year-old has zero wins in her last five and only one minor placing, all over 10f on similar going; Clifford Lee takes the ride but the consistent placed-without-winning profile and no recent upswing in form make this the most vulnerable runner in the field at current trajectory.|
runners_data.comment: Denied a clear run and ultimately eased after showing good speed at Ascot last time, which flatters the beaten margin considerably; acts well at 10f on any ground, and with genuine excuses for all his 2026 outings, first-time tongue-tie could spark a return to his previous best.

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and has won from the front over 10f on good ground; Ray Dawson rides and the mare's ability to dictate terms unchallenged is the defining tactical factor in this race — her chance is contingent on maintaining control of the fractions.|
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap at Epsom by six and a half lengths last time despite trouble in running, suggesting he operates at a higher level than his current mark reflects; acts on any ground and first-time hood adds intrigue, with a trainer in sharp form.

runners_data.name: Glacius
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old by nature wants to race prominently and has consistent placed form on good ground (4/4 sim-going record), but Billy Loughnane will find the position occupied ahead of him — racing without the prominent berth it wants, the style-fit discount is real and material.|
runners_data.comment: Hampered when a length and a quarter third in a Group 3 at Ascot last time, with his true level arguably understated by that result; stays 10f, acts on a sound surface and the trainer is in excellent form — plenty more to come from this one.

races.paceDynamic: Sallaal is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals over 1m2f at Sandown, shapes to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good ground — Roger Varian's mare has won from the front and is unlikely to be pressured into excess early fractions. Dividend and Boiling Point are natural prominent types who will seek to sit close to the pace, though the field contains more horses wanting that prominent position than the race shape can comfortably accommodate. Boiling Point and Glacius are genuine front-runners or close-up racers who are redistributed to a midfield mapping because Sallaal holds the lead and Dividend will contest the position immediately behind; both will be racing slightly out of their optimal role. With Sallaal likely to control an honest but unforced gallop and the prominent berths filled, this race shape strongly favours horses capable of tracking the pace in second or third — Dividend's consistent form on good ground over 10 furlongs makes it the profile that stands to benefit most, while true hold-up horses like Persica and Royal Rhyme face the task of generating momentum from further back in a race unlikely to set up for a late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sallaal Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Sallaal leads uncontested at a fair pace and the race is never truly run to suit hold-up types.
scenarios.body: If Sallaal leads uncontested at a fair pace and the race is never truly run to suit hold-up types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Dividend and Boiling Point both push forward early and force a contested pace just behind Sallaal.
scenarios.body: If Dividend and Boiling Point both push forward early and force a contested pace just behind Sallaal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sallaal sets an unexpectedly strong pace that stretches the field and leaves the lead wide open in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If Sallaal sets an unexpectedly strong pace that stretches the field and leaves the lead wide open in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Glacius Upsets the Pattern
scenarios.trigger: If Glacius, despite being redistributed from its natural prominent position, manages to track Sallaal closely and outstay older rivals.
scenarios.body: If Glacius, despite being redistributed from its natural prominent position, manages to track Sallaal closely and outstay older rivals.

watchPoints.text: Sallaal's early pace is the fulcrum of this entire race — if Ray Dawson goes off too slowly, Dividend or Boiling Point may elect to push up and disrupt the plan entirely, transforming the race shape.

Boiling Point and Glacius are both natural prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position behind Sallaal; watch for one or both to either drop back under restraint or create an unplanned mid-race surge if their riders choose to commit.

Persica's hold-up style under Ryan Moore depends entirely on a truly run race to close ground from the rear — with Sallaal likely to set only a fair pace, Moore may be forced to make an uncharacteristically early move or accept a non-competitive passage.

Royal Rhyme has not won in her last five starts and is 0W0P on similar going in recent history; Clifford Lee will need a marked step up in form for this horse to factor, making it primarily a market-movement watch rather than a tactical one.

races.name: Coral Marathon (Listed) (Registered As The Esher Stakes)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Connections know this track well and Ryan Moore's tactical intelligence is a positive, but this six-year-old's stable has sent out just one winner from 21 runners over the past fortnight and his five similar-going runs have produced zero wins and zero places at this trip; in this race he will be racing further off the pace than he naturally prefers, a consequence of the field being stacked with prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Beaten six lengths here in a Group 3 last time — a result that may overstate his current level slightly — yet today's 16f trip is at the heart of his ability and he acts well on good; first-time tongue-tie, though his trainer is in a lean spell.

runners_data.name: Furthur
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's in-form yard (12 from 57 over 14 days) and James Doyle booking lend confidence, and two wins and three places from his last 12 similar-going starts suggest he is well-suited to Good ground; at 15 days since his last run he is fresh, and his 2m Goodwood effort last time out — though finishing sixth — keeps him honest at the trip, making him the most natural threat to Lazy Griff if the leader weakens.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well down the field over an excessive distance at Ascot last time, but returns to a trip within his compass here; stays 14f well on a sound surface, and his stable having landed this race last year adds confidence, though a return to form is still to come.

runners_data.name: Lazy Griff
runners_data.note: The race's only true front-runner and likely to get an uncontested lead, which plays directly to his strengths; his recent hat-trick of placed efforts at 12-16f on Good going shows he is in excellent heart, and stepping up to 2m for the first time with Billy Loughnane aboard for Charlie Johnston's yard (9 from 67 over 14 days) is the key unknown, though the flat Sandown circuit mitigates any stamina concerns.
runners_data.comment: Acquitted himself well here last time on his return from a long absence, finishing two lengths third in a Group 3 over this course and distance; effective from 12f to 2m on a sound surface and looks to have further improvement to offer over staying trips.

runners_data.name: Paradias
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old veteran with Rossa Ryan aboard for Alan King (1 from 11 in 14 days), his five runs over similar going have yielded no wins or places at this trip, and his recent form figures of 3-1-3-5-5 show a mix of promise and inconsistency; he is a natural prominent type who sits toward the rear of the mapped field as a consequence of the field's composition rather than genuine hold-up tendencies, and that positional compromise is a meaningful handicap.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when beaten five lengths here last time, confirming his effectiveness over this course and distance; consistently holds his form, handles today's ground well and a trainer currently in good shape gives further confidence, though the first-rate opposition poses the challenge.

runners_data.name: Lady Vivian
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly carries a 5lb sex allowance but her Good-ground record is uninspiring — two sevenths from two runs — against more encouraging Soft-ground form; Hector Crouch takes the ride for a yard 5 from 36 in the past fortnight, and like Duke Of Oxford she will be racing a touch wider and further back than she would choose, the natural consequence of being one of several prominent runners competing for limited early real estate.
runners_data.comment: Back in better form when fourth at Baden-Baden on her most recent outing over a shorter trip, but this step up in distance is a question her form doesn't answer convincingly; usually consistent, yet she faces a stiff stamina test and a strong field here.

races.paceDynamic: Lazy Griff is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-strong field and should stride directly into a comfortable lead from the gate, setting a measured, uncontested gallop over Sandown's flat 2m trip on Good ground. With every other runner in the race a natural prominent type — Duke Of Oxford, Furthur, Paradias, and Lady Vivian all preferring to race close to the pace — there will be immediate pressure behind Lazy Griff as those horses jostle for position in the chasing group, though none is likely to seriously contest the lead itself. The field holds more prominent-running types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate: Duke Of Oxford and Lady Vivian are the runners most likely to find themselves racing a touch further back than ideal, while Furthur and Paradias may get closer to their natural slots tracking Lazy Griff. A controlled, single-file pace with a lone leader dictating comfortably on Good ground strongly favours front-running or close-tracking prominent types who can produce a sustained kick from the front over the final quarter-mile — patient hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged here as there are none to speak of, and closers pushed to the rear from redistributed prominent profiles will struggle to generate the momentum required.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lazy Griff Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lazy Griff is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a fair but measured pace that suits his stamina reserves over 2m.
scenarios.body: If Lazy Griff is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a fair but measured pace that suits his stamina reserves over 2m.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lazy Griff sets a genuinely testing gallop and ties himself up inside the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to reel him in.
scenarios.body: If Lazy Griff sets a genuinely testing gallop and ties himself up inside the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to reel him in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Oxford or Lady Vivian, despite racing further back than ideal, are able to secure a rail-hugging run and deliver a late sustained challenge on Good ground.
scenarios.body: If Duke Of Oxford or Lady Vivian, despite racing further back than ideal, are able to secure a rail-hugging run and deliver a late sustained challenge on Good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types fight for position early, creating a fractious early pace that disrupts the entire field and produces a truly run race.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types fight for position early, creating a fractious early pace that disrupts the entire field and produces a truly run race.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lazy Griff's position at the start — if Billy Loughnane is slow from the stalls or another runner pushes forward aggressively in the early furlongs, the uncontested lead that underpins the dominant scenario evaporates immediately.

Monitor Furthur's early positioning: if James Doyle slots him in directly behind Lazy Griff within the first half-mile, he becomes a clear danger to the leader's supremacy as the horse best placed to pounce if the pace becomes testing over the final three furlongs.

Duke Of Oxford with Ryan Moore is always capable of finding an economical route through a small field, and if the prominent horses ahead of him race keenly and burn each other out, his extra experience at the trip could make his redistributed position less of a disadvantage than the map suggests.

With all five runners broadly prominent in profile, watch for early jostling for rail position on the first bend — Sandown's 2m start can cause bunching as horses seek to avoid wide draws on the long run to the first turn, potentially unsettling Lady Vivian or Paradias who are already in compromised map positions.

races.name: JRA Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Arqoob
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who has finished second over 2m1f on Good ground; likely to lead uncontested and control fractions, though his OR of 87 means he carries the highest weight and will be vulnerable if the prominent racers track him closely and pounce late; the STYLE_FIT tag slightly tempers confidence in him holding on.
runners_data.comment: Capable in both codes and at home over today's extended trip, though first-time blinkers are a new variable after he ran too keenly in front at York last time and weakened. The current mark will stretch him, but form and distance say he can be involved.

runners_data.name: Minhad
runners_data.note: Strong similar-going record (9 runs, 2W, 4P) and a recent win over 12f on Good is the headline here; hold-up style suits a race where the pace could be genuinely honest, and Rossa Ryan is a booking worth noting for a trainer in good recent form (2/6 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Landed a head verdict at Thirsk two starts back off a mark 4lb lower than today's; last time was a more modest fifth, beaten 9 lengths off the same official mark. Off 51 days; a reliable type and the trainer is striking at a decent clip currently.

runners_data.name: Marnier
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden yard is firing (6/26 T14) which is the primary angle; won over 14f on Good and gets this trip, though his headgear (p — pacifier) and a recent run of 6th suggests he needs things to fall right; hold-up style is fine here if Arqoob sets a genuine gallop.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well at this course and distance last time, beaten only 2 lengths off a mark 1lb higher than today's when unable to get to the front. Top-rated on our figures, first-time cheekpieces, and a trainer with a strong course record give him clear appeal.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: The form line is the most pressing concern — 784 days off the track (23 jockeys flag) makes this an enormous question mark; has placed three times consecutively over 16f on Good before his absence, and Gary & Josh Moore are a sharp yard (5/33 T14), but his true hold-up style means he is squeezed into midfield on the map and may not get the run of the race he needs first time back.
runners_data.comment: Four consecutive unplaced efforts represent a concern, and a comfortable defeat in a hurdle at Fontwell last time adds to the caution. The combination of tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied for the first time may spark some improvement on the Flat, but he's one to watch rather than back.

runners_data.name: Macari
runners_data.note: Two wins over 14f in her record and good similar-going experience (10 runs, 2W, 5P) make her solid on paper; a natural hold-up runner who is repositioned to midfield given the cluster of closers in this field, and Rose Dawes's 5lb claim is worth noting, though the Sheena West yard is quiet (0/3 T14).
runners_data.comment: Well held on his latest visit here, beaten 6 lengths in a handicap having been well placed; his current mark looks stiff and he sits at the bottom of our figures. Trip and ground suit, but he needs to find more to figure.

runners_data.name: Aggagio
runners_data.note: Trainer Gary & Josh Moore have runners from both sides here; Aggagio's recent form shows 5th and 3rd and he has gone well on softer ground but his similar-going record on Good is modest (5 runs, 0W, 2P); a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position, and Jude Fernandes's 7lb claim only partially offsets the pace-shape disadvantage for a deep closer in this field.
runners_data.comment: A reliable Flat performer rated second in the field on our figures with a mark that suits this grade; his most recent third at Goodwood came after going off too sharply, which cost him in the closing stages. Ground and trip are no barrier.

runners_data.name: So Alex
runners_data.note: The most interesting profile in the race — two wins at 12f on Soft/Standard and two recent seconds on Good at 14f, progressive and lightly raced at four; Billy Loughnane is a strong jockey booking and he is likely to track Arqoob prominently, which is the ideal position if the front-runner begins to idle; similar-going record (3/9, 0W, 2P) is modest but the progressive form profile compensates.
runners_data.comment: Making genuine progress, he has won twice in his last five starts and performed with credit at staying distance for the first time at Carlisle last time, beaten three-quarters of a length off a mark just 1lb lower. Still with more to discover at this trip.

runners_data.name: Pyleates
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 66 and no wins or places on Good going from five runs on the surface; recent form of 3-7 is mixed and Saffie Osborne has a quiet book from this yard (0/16 T14); unknown style (U) adds uncertainty, though the 20-day break is not a concern in itself.
runners_data.comment: Related to top-level winner Pyledriver, and her mark may yet underestimate her potential; she encountered interference at a decisive stage last time here and was beaten 5 lengths without getting a clean run. A clearer passage could see a different result.

races.paceDynamic: Arqoob is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press him from the front, he is set to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop over 1m6f on Good ground at Sandown. So Alex and the original Arqoob profile will shape the prominent positions, but the field is notably rear-heavy: Galactic Jack, Macari, and Aggagio are all genuine hold-up horses yet are mapped to midfield because there is simply not enough room at the back for every closer to operate from their natural position — those three will struggle to get the ground they want behind the pace. With Arqoob likely to control fractions unchallenged and set a fair but unhurried tempo, the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who travel close to the gallop and have a sustained finish over this stamina trip — true deep closers needing a strong pace to get into the race are compromised by the lack of genuine forcing tactics.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arqoob Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Arqoob leads from the front at an honest but manageable gallop and no rival has the inclination to challenge him for the lead.
scenarios.body: If Arqoob leads from the front at an honest but manageable gallop and no rival has the inclination to challenge him for the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the tempo genuinely tests the prominent horses, allowing a deep closer to reel them in.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected and the tempo genuinely tests the prominent horses, allowing a deep closer to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Arqoob is allowed to dictate an uncontested crawl, building a substantial lead that the hold-up-heavy field cannot fully reel in.
scenarios.body: If Arqoob is allowed to dictate an uncontested crawl, building a substantial lead that the hold-up-heavy field cannot fully reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uneven with surges and slackening, turning the race into a war of attrition that suits a horse who travels strongly in the pack.
scenarios.body: If the pace is uneven with surges and slackening, turning the race into a war of attrition that suits a horse who travels strongly in the pack.

watchPoints.text: Arqoob sets the entire tempo — watch whether So Alex or any rider attempts to press him early, because if Arqoob is left alone in front the race effectively becomes a time trial and the closers will need a strong late burst to overhaul him.

Galactic Jack returns from 784 days off the track — watch his behaviour in the preliminaries and how quickly he settles early, as a horse this fresh could either run a career-best or capitulate; his previous form over 16f on Good is genuinely competitive if the layoff has not blunted him.

The midfield is congested with repositioned hold-up horses (Galactic Jack, Macari, Aggagio) — watch for traffic issues at the top of the straight where three horses looking for the same gap could interfere with each other's run.

Minhad's 51-day layoff after a win is worth monitoring in the paddock; the Ismail Mohammed yard is in recent form (2/6 T14) and if Minhad travels smoothly in the rear-to-midfield group he is the most classically suited hold-up horse to the scenario where Arqoob's gallop quickens late.

Pyleates's unknown running style (U) means her early positioning is genuinely unpredictable — if she breaks sharply and adds unexpected pressure to Arqoob's lead, the pace dynamic changes materially and the hold-up horses may benefit more than the scenarios currently price in.

races.name: Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Jamie Osborne, strong recent form including placed efforts over a mile on good ground — similar going record is modest (3 runs, no wins, one place) but trips are consistent; needs a genuine gallop to deliver his late run.|
runners_data.comment: A solid record at this trip on any going, but a well-below-form turf reappearance at York last time clouds the picture. Winless for close to three years, though consistent placings across that spell suggest he retains a decent level of ability at this distance.

runners_data.name: Triple Double A
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent racer has recorded three wins and four places from eight similar-going runs — solid record — and Billy Loughnane will aim to track Ascending Star closely from the outset; headgear (tongue-tie/plus) noted.|
runners_data.comment: Set off too freely at Nottingham last time and paid the price, beaten 10 lengths; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are designed to settle him and help him conserve his energy. Acts at this trip on good ground and has shown he can compete when ridden more patiently.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: Lightly turned around after just four days (last run), David Evans's visored runner has won three times at eight furlongs on good ground and Rossa Ryan is a strong booking; fresh running style (prominent) suits a well-organised race from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Won by three-quarters of a length at Salisbury three starts back and ran to his level last time, third beaten 4 lengths off the same mark. First-time visor for a gelding who handles good ground at this trip; quick return after just four days, and his inconsistency warrants care.

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly is a prominent type whose similar-going form is thin (three runs, no wins or places), though her one career win came at eight furlongs on soft; 7lb claimer Oliver Carmichael takes the ride with headgear (near-side hood).|
runners_data.comment: A step up on the run before when prevailing in a close handicap at Goodwood last time by half a length off a mark 2lb lower. First-time cheekpieces for a reliable type at this trip; the slight rise in official mark is the main question.

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner is a genuinely prominent-profile horse whose preferred position may be squeezed out by the volume of pace-inclined types — Sean Levey will need to be sharp from the gates; form figures include a placed effort on good at eight furlongs.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten only 3 lengths at York last time off a mark 1lb above today's, though he was caught for pace and it left the impression he'd be better served by a longer distance. Rated third in the field on our figures, he's on a potentially attractive mark with first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 1 and 3 at eight furlongs on good ground and comes here after 52 days off — front-running by nature but likely to find the early slots filled, meaning Rose Dawes (5lb) faces a tactical challenge to place the horse comfortably.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Lingfield last time, emptying quickly once challenged and showing little; rated second-lowest in the field on our figures. Off 52 days with first-time cheekpieces, and while the trip suits his best form, recent runs suggest the mark is too high.

runners_data.name: H Key Lails
runners_data.note: Attwater's consistent six-year-old has placed in his last four starts, including a recent win and two thirds at eight furlongs on standard; a natural forwardly-positioned runner, the 7lb claimer James Glennon will need early decisiveness to avoid being shuffled back.|
runners_data.comment: Thrived on a proactive ride when shortening in trip last time, taking a handicap at Lingfield by 3½ lengths off a mark 6lb lower than today's. Steps back up in distance today, a return he is respected for, and first-time cheekpieces suggest connections are managing the transition.

runners_data.name: Ascending Star
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and steps up to a mile after winning over the trip on good at Goodwood — Callum Rodriguez should lead comfortably; the uncontested role is a significant tactical asset at a weight-friendly 134lbs.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in trip after a break and won a novice at Lingfield by a length last time; the performance suggests he handles this distance well, and his initial handicap mark looks accessible. The trainer is in good form, and our figures place him top of the field.

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's genuine hold-up horse has a placed effort at seven furlongs and decent form on good — headgear (visor) worn — but requires a searching pace to get competitive; placed only twice from four similar-going runs and may find conditions too sedate.|
runners_data.comment: Has landed a race in France but his form since switching to British racing has been mixed; he had difficulty with the Brighton track on his most recent start. First-time visor for a gelding effective at this trip on sound going, though more is needed.

runners_data.name: Chilly Breeze
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's hold-up horse has never won and shows modest form figures across seven similar-going runs, consistently failing to land a blow; Ryan Kavanagh (5lb) rides but the lack of a strong pace will leave this runner with little chance of getting involved.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled wide by a tricky draw at Chester most recently and well beaten, though the sharp nature of that track may have hindered him; acts on good ground at 7f. Rated last in the field on our figures with a trainer who has fired just once in 28 recent runners.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly raced three-year-old has placed in both completed starts at seven furlongs on good/standard and steps up to a mile — unknown running style, but Hector Crouch is experienced enough to improvise; 52-day absence is a minor query but the form profile is tidy.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up twice in her last three starts, including at Lingfield most recently when beaten 2 lengths but tending to pull hard. Off 52 days; second-highest-rated on our figures and the potential for further progress on her handicap bow makes her a genuine threat.

races.paceDynamic: Ascending Star is the confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine lead horse in the field, will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset and control a measured, sustainable gallop over Sandown's flat mile. Triple Double A, Dovey Moon, and Silca Bay are the natural prominent types who will attempt to sit just behind the leader, creating a bunched and competitive early order rather than a ragged, strung-out field. The redistribution note is important here: Cristo, Special Ghaiyyath, and H Key Lails are all true prominent horses by style but the field cannot accommodate them all in their preferred positions, meaning at least some will be shuffled back further than they would like, compromising their chances. With Ascending Star able to dictate an uncontested, honest-but-not-suicidal pace, this race shape most favours horses who can sit close to the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent types who travel smoothly into the straight will hold a material edge over genuine hold-up horses who need a strong pace to chase.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ascending Star Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ascending Star leads at a comfortable clip and the field settles into a rhythm behind without disruption.
scenarios.body: If Ascending Star leads at a comfortable clip and the field settles into a rhythm behind without disruption.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotly Contested
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types dispute early for position behind Ascending Star, lifting the tempo and creating genuine pace.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types dispute early for position behind Ascending Star, lifting the tempo and creating genuine pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle sections to bring the genuine hold-up horses into the finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle sections to bring the genuine hold-up horses into the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Disruption Favours Unexposed
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for early position causes Cristo or Special Ghaiyyath to lose their place entirely, scrambling the tactical picture in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the scramble for early position causes Cristo or Special Ghaiyyath to lose their place entirely, scrambling the tactical picture in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Dovey Moon's four-day turnaround is unusually short — if she is not fully recovered from her last run, Rossa Ryan may find her flat when asked to quicken, reversing what looks like a well-placed favourite candidate.

Cristo, Special Ghaiyyath, and H Key Lails are all natural front-of-race horses crammed into the same tactical space — watch the first furlong for barging or crowding as all three try to secure position behind Ascending Star.

Ascending Star's recent form (three runs only, progressing fast) means her ability to control a mile at Sandown for a full eight furlongs is unproven — if she weakens earlier than expected, the scenario shifts dramatically toward the hold-up horses.

Thursday Girl is 0W1P from three runs but has been placed twice stepping up in trip each time — watch whether Ed Walker has targeted this race for a forward move, as lightly raced improvers can be underestimated in competitive flat handicaps.

T14 strike rates are broadly unremarkable across the field except Richard Hannon (10/50) — Cristo may have been placed here with specific intent, making Sean Levey's ability to navigate the positional congestion a key watch point in the first two furlongs.
